common_name: Snow Azalea (Historic Pure White Kurume Azalea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, acidic (pH 4.5-6.0), humus-rich soil in partial shade; Snow is one of the original Kurume azalea selections introduced to the West by plant collector E.H. Wilson in 1918.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade with good air circulation. Snow is one of E.H. Wilson's original Kurume azalea introductions brought from Japan to the West in 1918, valued for over a century for its dense, compact, fine-textured habit and abundant small, pure white single flowers that cover the shrub in a heavy spring flush. Its small leaves and tight, mounding form give it the refined, formal appearance typical of the best Kurume selections, and its long track record in Southern gardens speaks to its reliability. Water deeply during dry spells, especially while establishing, and prune lightly right after flowering if shaping is needed, since flower buds for next year's bloom set soon after the spring flush ends.
sources: University of Georgia Cooperative Extension — Azalea Cultivars for the Landscape
Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Azaleas for Texas Gardens
